source.title: Why Lottery Ticket Wins? A Theoretical Perspective of Sample Complexity on Pruned Neural Networks
source.authors: Shuai Zhang; Meng Wang; Sijia Liu; Pin-Yu Chen; Jin-Jun Xiong

record.tranche_reason: The paper gives theoretical and empirical results about pruning and generalization, using an oracle-learning setup and test error or accuracy rather than the claim versions’ specified tests.
record.gate_note: The paper does not test random-label memorization, width sweeps, architecture comparisons, adaptive optimizers, batch size, dropout, magnitude-aware sharpness, or removal of memorized examples. Its pruning results concern test performance and sample complexity; they do not directly test any listed version.
record.test_reason: The study tests pruning, oracle recovery and sample complexity, but none of V1–V8. Pruning weights is neither widening past interpolation nor removing memorized training examples; local convexity is not magnitude-aware sharpness correlated with generalization gaps.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors establish recovery and sample-complexity guarantees for one-hidden-layer ReLU oracle models with Gaussian inputs and accurate masks, interpreting these as an explanation for winning-ticket generalization. Experiments extend the investigation to inaccurate masks and deeper image classifiers, with excessive pruning degrading performance.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies pruning and oracle-model recovery, not the claim versions’ interventions or measurements. Its theoretical training method is accelerated gradient descent; empirical pruning uses GraSP and IMP.
record.method_sensitivity: Pruning ratio, mask accuracy, and training sample count affect reported test performance; excessive pruning worsens it.

fits_no_version.finding: Proper pruning improves held-out performance in the tested synthetic, MNIST and CIFAR-10 settings; excessive pruning worsens performance. Synthetic results also depend on mask accuracy and sample count.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Suitable weight pruning can reduce the number of training examples needed to attain a given held-out performance, but its benefits depend on pruning extent and mask quality.

record.problems: The theoretical analysis assumes one hidden layer, Gaussian inputs, an accurate mask, and an oracle-learner setup. The deeper-network experiments are limited to MNIST and CIFAR-10; the text gives trends but not exact plotted test values or uncertainty for those figures.
record.rows_left_out: No additional results bearing on the listed versions were reported. The figures in Sections 4.1–4.3 also report optimization convergence, sample complexity, initialization success, and model-estimation errors; these do not measure the listed claim versions’ outcomes.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance compared with natural labels.
Width increases beyond the zero-training-error threshold and their effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and compensating training recipes.
Dropout effects, including training-set size, excessive dropout and augmentation interactions.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, its association with generalization gaps and its ranking against other measures.
Removing examples selected by label memorization versus removing equal numbers of random examples.

record.verdict_notes: References to original sources provide background rather than tests or operational uses of their claim versions. The local-convexity results do not establish V7. No verdict labels apply.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label fitting or comparison of natural-label and random-label generalization.
No width sweep around the zero-training-error threshold.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.
No adaptive optimizer versus SGD comparison on held-out performance.
No magnitude-aware sharpness measurement or comparison with generalization gaps.
No removal of examples selected for memorization.

rows.subject: Algorithm 1 learned model; synthetic oracle data
rows.operation_detail: Varied pruning ratio and training sample size using IMP; measured test error.
rows.value: For fixed N greater than 100, test error decreases as pruning ratio increases; when pruning ratio is greater than 80%, test error is large for all N.
rows.note: The text describes the curve trends but does not give individual plotted values.
rows.check: The reported pruning trends are supported, but do not measure any listed version, so partial is inappropriate. Add that N = 100 performs poorly throughout and that the synthetic noise level is 0.001 relative to noiseless output RMS.
